utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. And good afternoon, everybody. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. All the Defence teams are here minus Ms. Nikolic. All right. Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer for the Prosecution. The witness is present. Mr. Haynes, perhaps you can continue and conclude with your -- conclude your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, if you don't mind, I'm going to start by tidying up two or three things. Firstly, yesterday we were talking about some areas or some villages or towns that fell within the defence zone of the Romanija Brigade, and what I wanted to clarify with you was that according to your definition of the defence zone, the towns of Sokolac and Han Pijesak do not fall within it. Do you understand what I'm suggesting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question, but the municipalities of Sokolac and Han Pijesak did fall within the area of defence. The area or the zone had as its boundaries the forward defence line, the right flank, the left flank and it is also determined by its depth, which means that it went as far as the positions of the combat elements of the brigade were stationed. The elements of the rear or logistics structures were far back into the depth of the zone. Therefore, the territories of the municipalities of Sokolac and Han Pijesak were within the zone of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's my mistake. I should have stuck with the word "towns." It's the towns that were not within the zone of defence of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those that were not within that area were not within that competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And perhaps you can correct a mistake I made at the end of yesterday's sitting, which was I showed you some rules relating to asanacija from 1991 and of course those were rules of the JNA and not the VRS. You'd agree with that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I observed that but I didn't make any comments on that. The instructions were issued as those of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, a question I meant to ask you at the very outset, you were injured in combat on the 29th of July; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sometime prior to that, you had replaced the Zvornik Brigade forces at Zepa under Vinko Pandurevic, who had left the area to return to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you can confirm, can you, that no time after the Zvornik Brigade forces left Zepa did you ever see Vinko Pandurevic in that area again?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't see him in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Nor did you see any forces of the Zvornik Brigade in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't see a single unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I want to return briefly to a document I showed you yesterday, which is P106, so if that could be put into e-court, please. And I want you to look at the paragraph again which I asked you to look at yesterday, which is paragraph 2, and I want you to, if you can, assess the size of the total force from that information, which was sent to perform operation Krivaja 95. And I would ask you to agree, if you do, that that represents a total force of something like 12 to 1500 men.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this document and the assignments issued to the 1st Zvornik, to the Bircani, Romanija, and Vlasenica brigades, the figure would be just about what you said, because a company numbers up to 200 men. A light battalion would be at the strength of two reinforced companies. In that case, precisely that conclusion can be drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to confirm, which we can read in English anyway, that the Zvornik Brigade contribution to that force was a light battalion plus additional logistical support?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, according to your understanding, that meant that the force that was sent to conduct operation Krivaja 95, facing the forces within Srebrenica, was outnumbered five or six to one; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outnumbered by the forces of the 28th Division that were there? Is that the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the area of your axis of attack and the axis of the Zvornik Brigade was rather easier to defend than it was to attack; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any event, it was easier, given the lie of the land and the time that the 28th Division had spent in that area, which gave it ample opportunity to organise its defences.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you agree that progress in separating -- in firstly separating the enclaves was slow and difficult?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any attack and movement of units in an offensive against a well-organised defence, as indeed was something that we came across in the enclave, is definitely very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were the forces of the 28th Division particularly strong and determined on the axis of the Zvornik Brigade unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the combat activities that my right adjacent unit experienced, that was definitely something much fiercer than in the area where I engaged my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it's correct, isn't it, that on the 10th of July, the forces of the Zvornik Brigade were driven back by the forces of the 28th Division to their starting place?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you were aware that those forces suffered losses in that counteroffensive?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that, in the evening briefing we had, that my neighbours had experienced losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: By contrast, on the 11th of July, when the task had changed to move into Srebrenica, you noticed that your neighbours were failing to move forward in the face of almost no opposition; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were quite a few problems experienced in view of the terrain and the resistance we came across and the Birac Brigade, my left adjacent unit, also experienced losses. I was later on informed by Colonel Andric that his unit had experienced losses. Therefore, resistance was still mounted out of some positions and strongholds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It may not -- it may be that you didn't understand my question. What I was suggesting to you is that you noticed on the 11th of July that Legenda was slow in moving forward, despite the fact that the enemy was very quiet.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself issued some requests in that regard because elements of my unit were successful in seizing certain elevation points and in advancing somewhat more speedily. In that context I sent a request to Legenda, or rather, to his soldiers that I came across along that axis to get more actively involved in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And lastly in relation to those events, you were very close to the vehicle struck by NATO bombs on the 11th of July, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was, and it is from that time that my injury to the right ear dates. I wasn't directly hit. Rather, my ear -- hearing was impaired by the detonation I was near.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think you were able to see what sort of vehicles it were that were struck by those bombs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some vehicles were struck. There were some command vehicles with communications equipment mounted on them, some combat vehicles that were following the combat formations but were not directly engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, if you don't mind waiting a few seconds, I'm going to ask you that see a little bit of video now about some forces that you encountered in Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you play it now, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry about this, Mr. Trivic. It's a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't appear we are going to be able to achieve that, so I'm going to have to jog your memory in a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suggest that you may proceed with jogging his memory. In the meantime, the technicians will try -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. President, we may also be able to assist if we're given a cite if it's on Sanction the Srebrenica trial video, it's that exhibit and you've got a time, we can cue it up as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But please do proceed with your line of questions trying to jog his memory in the meantime --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and then if you need the video, we go to it, if not, we jump to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think during the course of your interview with the Office of the Prosecution, you were shown some stills of a video of Srebrenica town centre which featured soldiers wearing black uniforms, who were taking a flag and putting it in a receptacle of some sort. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very specific question with regard to that footage, and I didn't pay attention to that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I'll have to leave that to one side and we'll have to come back to it. Ah, thank you very much. Somebody has a still of it. Can I show you this and maybe we can put it on the ELMO. Do you remember seeing this photograph before?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing soldiers dressed like this in Srebrenica town centre on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, you can see they've got numbers on them. They have been identified for us in this and other proceedings and we know that they are members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. Was that a unit that formed any part of the force that performed operation Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units that were listed in the command for active combat did not include this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there any military requirement on the 11th of July for any further units to join your force in Srebrenica town centre?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In that event, then I'll move on. Now, during the course of your evidence, you've told us about a meeting which you attended in the evening at the command of the Bratunac Brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we be clear at the outset that you attended one meeting and one meeting only at the Bratunac Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: According to you, the people who were there included the following: Generals Mladic and Krstic, Colonels Blagojevic and Pandurevic, and yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generals Mladic and Krstic, the then Colonel Pandurevic, and I. I said that I wasn't sure whether Blagojevic was present. I seem to recall seeing him that evening. I don't know whether it was at the meeting or not. I made a note of that and I'm sure about that, that Pandurevic was there because I remembered his reaction to the assignment issued. This is something that I consistently stated in my earlier statements. All the subordinate officers should have been there, just as I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, you've pre-empted my next question, which is, presumably you agree that there were other people there but you just can't remember who they are now; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't give you individual names of the people who were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And presumably you'd also agree that you saw other people outside the meeting at the command of the Bratunac Brigade on the night that you went to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one I encountered was the officer in the operations room who directed me to the room where the meeting was to take place, over dinner, were the people who I met that day but I cannot give you the specific names.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, let me see if I can jog your memory. Do you remember whether Colonel Andric was there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I cannot be specific about anyone else except for Colonel Blagojevic and Generals Mladic and Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You're now specific about Colonel Blagojevic, are you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how shall I put it to you. I am not sure whether he was there throughout the meeting, but I -- as far as I can remember, I did see him that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What about Colonel Nastic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time he was a major. The same applies to him. I cannot say for sure. They were supposed to be there, just like myself and Pandurevic. It is possible that they had asked for permission for someone to stand in for them and attend in their place, but I can't give you all the specific names. He should have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one more: Major Jevdjevic, do you remember if he was there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you know Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you saw him in the command of the Bratunac Brigade on the night you were at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to, if you don't mind, read you some descriptions of a meeting and see whether they sound familiar to you as the meeting you were at. And the first is the description of General Krstic, and if anybody wants to know, it's IT 9833, page 6575, lines 11 to 20. "The meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters started at around 2200 hours. The meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters was attended by General Mladic, General Zivanovic. I was there, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade was there, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic. Then there was the commander the Birac Brigade, Colonel Andric; the commander of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, Colonel Trivic; the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Colonel Blagojevic; the commander of the Milici Brigade, Major Nastic. Then there was Major Jevdjevic, commander of the battalion, the communications battalion of the Drinski corps." He's asked a question and it's at that meeting that you were given your assignment to command the Zepa battle group; is that right? Does that sound like the meeting you went to?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to read you something else. This is from the interview of Momir Nikolic which is in e-court as 7D425. It's page 25 in e-court but I'm not going to put it up. "After the meeting, which did not last long, the commanding officers came out and they discussed the new task. What I learned was that the task was about the forces which participated Srebrenica were to be transferred to Zepa. That was one thing that I learned. The following day, the following was that they did not manage to reach an agreement about that and the reason was simply that there were no intelligence, there was no reliable information regarding the location of the column, I'm referring to the Muslim column, about the movement, about the further targets and that because of that, one of the participants, and this part I learned later, complained and they did not accept Mladic's idea to move to Zepa." He's asked by Mr. McCloskey, in fact: "Which participant complained?" And he replies: "I heard it was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Pandurevic." Isn't that the meeting you were describing to us earlier this week?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does sound like the meeting that I attended, in terms that Colonel Pandurevic launched an initiative that this task be not -- not be carried out and that rotation of troops be facilitated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm now going to read you something from an interview with Milenko Jevdjevic. This is also in e-court but I'll read it to you. What he said when being interviewed by Mr. Ruez was, "Yes, I was present but that meeting remained because I received an order to go to Krivaca. That means they got together. I don't know if following that, after I went, but it was logical to expect they had a meeting. I was ordered at once to set up a communications centre at Krivaca because the task was to transfer all the units immediately to Zepa." And in relation to who was there, he says, "The commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Pandurevic; and I think the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Vidoje Blagojevic; the commander of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, Trivic; the commander of the Milici Brigade, Nastic." At the meeting you attended, was somebody ordered to set up a forward command post in relation to the operation at Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make a note of that. I wouldn't like to guess. But I suppose that a task for a new command post should have been assigned but only after the task given to General Krstic. If it happened that on that evening the commander of the Krivaja 95 operation was said that the operation will be continued towards Zepa, logically to follow would be an order to the corps to be transferred to a new area. This is my view and what I would normally expect, according to the rules of engagement for the activities to be directed in that course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In any event, you will notice that all three of those people describe a meeting that includes all the people you recall being there, and you. So it must have been the meeting you were at because you were only at one, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a meeting where a reaction was put forth to the continuation of the activities, and the decision on this operation was to be made by 8.00 the next day. Judging by Colonel Pandurevic's reaction and my support of his reaction did not entail any changes. General Mladic was then expected to address the soldiers the following day and to boost their motivation for the task at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, each of those people, General Krstic, Momir Nikolic and Miljenko Jevdjevic, describe a meeting which they say took place on the 11th of July at which you were present. Do you think they might be right about the date and you might be wrong?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my notebook, in which I recorded some crucial activities of mine, this is what it was and this is how it's written. If it happens to be some different date, then that would mean that my whole records were wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can look into that a little bit. It would have been natural, wouldn't it, to have had a meeting of the commanding officers on the night of a victory, and it would have been according to protocol for there to be congratulations, a celebratory meal and a debriefing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not disputing that this would be only natural, but I went to this meeting after I had come to the Jahorina feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And isn't that what General Mladic was ordering everybody to do at about 6.00 in the evening in Srebrenica? He was telling everybody to forget history, go on to Bratunac. That was his order, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic did not issue assignments to commanders but rather to units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Forgive me, Mr. Trivic, but in discussing your encounter with General Mladic in Srebrenica, you said it was not a conversation because he was a superior officer. Did you not regard it as an order that he was telling everybody to go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me about General Mladic, he would often, in his encounter with people and one-on-one meetings, issue some tasks just in passing and he never later checked whether they were carried out or not. He never insisted on any other procedure than the one applied. I just drew it to his attention that I was carrying out the task immediately after receiving the order of that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we'll move on from that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you'll allow me just one more sentence, it wasn't to be expected for him to order the commander of the brigade -- issue the commander -- order the brigade commanders of the Drina Corps to come to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, according to your testimony, at the meeting you attended, there was no discussion about the separation of men of military age from their families at Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But one thing you do recall is General Mladic either making or receiving a telephone call; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He talked to someone on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, on your way to Bratunac on the evening that you went to this meeting, you passed through Potocari. You told us that. Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you didn't see any buses in Potocari on the evening that you passed through it, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the telephone conversation that you heard General Mladic making involved him seeking to procure vehicles for the transport of the population at Potocari, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I remember from that conversation was that General Mladic insisted with the person he was talking to that his party, his interlocutor, provide fuel, whereas he, or the army, was going to provide vehicles for the transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. The phrase I picked up from your evidence the other day was that General Mladic said he would make sure the buses were there. Is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, vehicles, buses, and other conveyances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So it was your impression of that conversation that it was an arrangement to commence the transportation of people from Potocari, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One may arrive at that conclusion. There was mention of the transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there also mention at this meeting of the fact that Mladic and Momir Nikolic had attended a meeting at the Hotel Fontana the same evening?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there mention of the fact that the -- there had been discussion earlier that evening with general -- Colonel Karremans about the provision of buses by the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If we are now able, I'd like to show you a section of video, please, of Potocari. It's V 0004458, 831 to 923, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's enough for my purposes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I'm interested to know how did you drive through Potocari on the 12th of July and not see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to read what I stated and to make your own conclusions. I never said that I had never seen people in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, but you said you didn't see buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think to be fair to the witness, if my learned friend has some time frame in mind for this piece of footage on the 12th, that might be a little more fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's see if the witness has an explanation first, because he may have in mind some time frame himself. If not, I suggest Mr. Haynes --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to move on, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Let's give him the opportunity now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because you've thrown the question at him and I think it's fair enough, especially in light of the objection raised or the remark that he be given the opportunity to explain, give any explanation. Do you have any explanation to give us, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I don't remember that on the 12th, on the way to the meeting, I noticed the buses, but I also said that on the 13th I did see buses, trailer trucks and other conveyances, and I don't know what else I can change in my statement. I said I didn't remember. You can show me a footage and I can say yes, you're right, they were there, but I personally don't remember. I do remember that on the 13th, while passing through Srebrenica and Potocari, on my way to my new task, I did see all of that, and after all, I was being driven in a vehicle that was part of that convoy. I couldn't have passed by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Will you proceed, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, my next question is this: Can you imagine why, on the evening of the 12th of July, if you are correct, General Mladic would have been having a conversation with somebody on the telephone to arrange the commencement of transport from Potocari when it had already been going on all day and he had plenty of buses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object on a couple of grounds. Number 1, the term "imagine" just is begging for speculation at this point. He's testified both on direct, previously on cross about his recollection of the events and the timing of the events and what he remembers happened. So I think we are beginning to waste time on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'll put the question another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's hear the different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Given what you know about the conversation you heard, do you not think it's more likely that you heard that conversation on the night of the 11th of July rather than the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot make any assessments of that kind. I stand by what I said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If I told you that we have video in this case of a conversation between Colonel Karremans and General Mladic in which they discuss the provision of transport by the United Nations earlier on the evening of the 11th, would that not make sense of the conversation you heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, objection, Your Honour. This is just trying it from a different angle. The questions are repetitive and we are not moving the ball along at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if you wish to comment, do so, by all means, Mr. Haynes. On the other hand, I think you pressed the matter for already about two or three minutes, and the latest you've heard from the witness is that he stands by what he has stated earlier. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if you wish to pursue the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, no, no. We'll move on, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: One of the other things you've told us about the meeting you attended is that there was no information available at this meeting about the whereabouts and the movement of the Muslim column; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at what I said. I don't remember any details pertaining to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you now: Was there any information available at the meeting you attended about the whereabouts or the movement of the Muslim column?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that during the first day of my stay here, I said a few things about this, and that is that each meeting usually begins with the information about what's going on in the combat area, but I myself didn't note this information down, nor did I memorise any specifics. It would have been normal procedure for the superior officer to brief those in attendance about the current events and developments in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's a simple enough question, Mr. Trivic. I'm going to ask it one more time. At the meeting you attended, was there any information about the whereabouts or the movement of the Muslim column?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only make an assessment, and on the basis of this assessment an order was produced to units to undertake security measures in their respective areas, security measures for roads alongside with members of the Ministry of the Interior, MUP. Based on that, the assessment was that the units were to move towards Tuzla, towards the forces of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask you be shown a few documents now, then. Could P1100 be put into e-court? And I think the best copy for the witness to look at is probably D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just to be -- I'm trying to be quick on this, no broadcast for the time being of this document. The point to be made is that I am informed that this is a document which, to our knowledge, is for the time being under seal. You can of course make reference to it, but we are not to show it to the public. And if you're going to mention any particular names from that document, please consult with us in private session before you do so, so that we decide if to proceed in private session then or in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I think it's sufficient for my purposes that the document is simply not broadcast. There are no names in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I haven't seen it, so...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's not the same document. Can we try 1101? I appear to have a different document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is no 1101.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, can we go to 1103, then, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. A is the English and D would be the best copy for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, just so you understand this, Mr. Trivic, this is a record of an intercepted conversation between two members of the army of Republika Srpska, and according to this, one of them is in fact a general, and it takes -- it took place at 7.48 in the morning of the 12th of July. And can you see it begins, "Hello, yes, general, I spoke with Mane." And if you read down, you'll see it refers halfway down to, "You've probably been informed a big column of Turks has started to arrive in Raince. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was any information of that sort made available at the meeting you went to?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, wasn't Colonel Pandurevic in particular concerned about information as to where the 28th Division might have gone at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume he was. In order to reach the area of Kladanj and Tuzla from the Srebrenica area, one had to go across the area of defence of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But no information was available as to where they were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to try it a couple more of these. Can we go back to 1100 A, please? Now, this is another intercepted communication which took place at 6.56 in the morning of the 12th of July. And you can see it's between again two members of the army of Republika Srpska and they are saying to another,"Hello, yes, they are moving in groups of 100 from Jaglici over there between me and the Milici men. They are moving over here towards Bokcin and Potok so they'll probably go down there towards Kamenica and Pobudje. Since there's an inhabited Serb village at the Milici, the only possibility they have is to go down towards Kamenica. We've been following that column, or rather several of those columns, since 3.00 this morning." Now, at the meeting you attended, was there any information that the column was being monitored by anybody?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I say that I don't remember any details, and if it in no way affected the area covered by the 2nd Romanija Brigade, then the reason why this did not stick in my memory is not that this may not have been mentioned but, rather, that I simply don't remember. At any rate, the commanders of the units who were tasked with securing roads and who were to apply heightened measures of combat readiness on their positions were supposed to be wary of surprise attacks, which were expected to come from the forces of the 28th Division who were supposed to link up with their units. This means that some concern was present but not on my part, and I did not pay particular attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we look at one more, 1106 A, please? Again, D would be the best copy for the witness. Is the document in front of you, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it in the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think it's now before you in your language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This too is protected. So no broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You here see that this is a conversation between the duty officer at Badem, that's the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, and Zlatar, that's the Drina Corps command, and here, one of the co-locutors, as we call them, says, "They are moving up towards Konjevic Polje and Kosat. We have information it's exactly like that. What action did you take, for God's sake? Listen, General Krstic is here." Now, did General Krstic mention at the meeting that were you at anything about where this column was and where it was going?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one more, P112 A -- 1121 A -- sorry -- and C would be the best copy for the witness this time. Is it in front of you in your language, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Does the name Obrenovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two men I knew by the name of Obrenovic. This was -- there was one who was the commander of Bratunac Brigade and the other was the Chief of Staff of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, whoever it was, did the meeting you attended receive any information that Obrenovic had captured a Turk?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Or that the column was moving towards Lolici?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: One last thing, Mr. Trivic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it is important, but I'm not sure whether the witness has seen that part of the entire --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's been drawn to my attention is that this intercept is at the bottom of the page, it's the one at 1640, so it perhaps ought to be wound down so he has the chance to briefly look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He can see it now, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just this last thing on this topic, Mr. Trivic: Do you think it is remotely conceivable that a meeting held on the evening of the 12th of July would not have received all this detailed information about the movement of the Muslim column?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I will give you the same answer. If at this meeting the units were ordered to secure roads, then at the beginning of the meeting, information must have been given to the effect that the forces of the 28th Division were heading toward the Tuzla canton, not a canton at the time, but at any rate that they were going toward their own units, leaving this area, and that it was certain that they would pass through the areas of defence of certain brigades on their way. In accordance with that, the assignments of the units was to secure these roads in order that the units which were supposed to be reassigned and redeployed to other areas can do so safely and securely. I do not recall any specific mention of this at the meeting. These matters may have been discussed but I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, the day after this meeting, you had lunch at the command of the Bratunac Brigade; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you told us on the 21st, that's two days ago, that you left the command of the Bratunac Brigade at about 5.00 or 1700 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left at around 5.00, I think I said, which made it possible for me to be in the area where my unit was assigned to by 6.00. We were supposed to deploy there and take up positions for the new mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, it may not be important, but I thought you said the other day that it made it possible for you to return to your unit by 7.00, but there it is. What time did you pass through Potocari on your way from Bratunac on the day after this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, when you left Bratunac at 5.00, you headed towards your unit, and the other day you told us that you passed through Potocari for the last time. I'm asking you what time you passed through Potocari, if you left Bratunac at 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently you misunderstood me. You didn't put the question properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, I think there is a mistake of fact embedded in the question that may be confusing the witness concerning where he was when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then I think the witness was about to explain it, if you are correct. Go ahead, Mr. Trivic. You had just started telling Mr. Haynes that he evidently had misunderstood you. Can you explain why, please? And then we see whether it's the case of proceeding with the question or having it rephrased.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that Mr. Haynes tied up two different events. One part of his question has to do with my departure from the meeting and then the other part of the question has to do with my new mission and my going through Potocari on my way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, let's just get this clear. It's probably my fault, Mr. Trivic. You left Bratunac on the -- what you say was the 13th of July at 5.00 in the afternoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be specific. I will give you the specific route I took. From the Jasenova command post, I set out to issue assignments to my unit to march along the road that was approved and to reach the area of Krivaca by 1900 hours. Next, I set out with my vehicle, belonging to the command, across Srebrenica and Potocari. I dropped by the Bratunac Brigade command in passing, had lunch there, and reached the area of Krivaca at 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, all I'm asking you is to tell me what time it was you passed through Potocari for the last time that day.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day I passed through Potocari only once, after I had issued assignments to my unit, I don't know the exact time, around 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Forgive me, but I understood you to have said the other day that when you had finished your lunch in Bratunac, you went back through Potocari. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But in any event, when you went through Potocari on the afternoon of the 13th of July, as you believe it to have been, you saw a lot of people and a lot of buses and people getting on to buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stated that several times, not only buses but also trailer trucks, lorries, even smaller ones without tarpaulin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And many, many thousands of people?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speculate. At any rate, large numbers of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, please help me. Would you have said thousands?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly even more, several thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You see, would it interest you to know that the evidence we've heard from Dutch soldiers is that the transportation of people from Potocari finished at about 5.00 on the afternoon of the 13th of July? I'll ask you again do you not think that your whole notes on this event are one day out and in fact what you described is passing through Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on the 13th, I was marching along Jasenova, Srebrenica, Potocari, Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Han Pijesak, Krivaca route. Along that route, independently of the meeting, along that route on the 13th, when the unit was redeployed, and as I came to the new area, I saw what I stated, both to you and to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was what you saw a scene like you watched in that video just now, of people being loaded on to buses?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw people being loaded on the buses, and I travelled together with the convoy of trailer trucks, buses and conveyances holding people. There were more people still in Potocari. I do not rule out the possibility that people were being loaded on the 12th as well. I never ruled that possibility out. I only said when it was that I observed that. On the evening of the 12th, I returned, or rather, in the afternoon, I returned after I had transported those two grandmothers. Upon my return, I took a grandfather, or rather, not I but a driver of mine, he was found in an abandoned camp where the members of the 28th Division must have been staying. As my unit approached that area, those forces retreated, leaving that grandfather behind. The grandfather was asking, pleading with us, to kill him because he had been abandoned by his sons. I ordered the driver to take him over to Potocari. On the 12th, on my way to the meeting, I gave a lift to two grandmothers. On the 13th, I saw what I said I saw. But I do not rule out the possibility that on the 12th, people were being loaded on to vehicles. I said that I heard General Mladic speaking to someone about fuel on the 12th. This conversation need not necessarily mean that there were insufficient vehicles. I don't recall the details of the conversation. On the basis of what I observed and on the basis of the notes I made, that is what I believe. I don't believe that I was off the mark in my notes that much. I believe that I noted the events of the 13th correctly and that this indeed happened on that date that I went through Potocari on my way to that new area of deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I believe I've concluded my cross-examination, but I'd just like to consult with my client before formally closing it but those are all the questions I've got for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can have the break now. It will be of 20 minutes, 25 minutes duration, and after that you will tell us whether you have concluded or not. Is someone else going to cross-examine this witness further? Okay. All right. Okay. So 25 minutes break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, since we were given the indication that we were going to have one hour and a half and that would cover the totality of the cross-examinations and it doesn't seem to be so now, please sit down again during the break and see what's going to happen. We would like to know how long you expect to be cross-examining the witness, because you had anticipated two and a half hours for the next witness plus maybe the rest of the time for his cross-examination but, anyway...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we continue with the cross-examinations, can someone enlighten us on what's going to happen? Let's start from here. We have Popovic team is going to cross-examine. How much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Less than that, Your Honours. Maybe two questions, three questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Less than that? Ten minutes, what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: At the most, Your Honour, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Five minutes, maximum ten, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe there will be any cross-examination from our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Miletic? She's not ready. Miletic? Madam Fauveau. She's done. You're done, yes. And Gvero is done and Pandurevic is done, so we've got another maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sadly, no. I've got three questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I thought you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, no. I was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just checked that I hadn't missed anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HAYNES
utterances.text: -- with your client, yes, you are 100 per cent right. So let's continue, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Near the end, Mr. Trivic. We've seen a little bit of video footage of you and General Mladic and other officers in Srebrenica town centre on the 11th of July. You recall watching that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in that footage, we saw that General Mladic was very keen that everybody should go on to Potocari. You recall, I imagine, him saying that at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you recall whether anybody tried to dissuade him from that particular idea?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you remember who that was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the person, but I know that somebody said that it wouldn't be a good idea to proceed further with the units in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at just a little bit of videotape now, please, if you would, and see if that reminds you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we stop the tape there? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Does that remind you as to who it was that tried to dissuade General Mladic from going on to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And are you aware whether, in accordance with what he said to General Mladic, in fact the units of Pandurevic were then employed trying to secure the hills?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After this intervention or warning, all units proceeded to carry out their tasks even in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did those units include the units of the Drina Wolves commanded by Legenda or Major Jolovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were part of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, I first wanted to ask you to give me an answer to what you already responded to last -- about Zepa. We have information that elements of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think all the elements, but those who did not withdraw from the area were at Koliba, Zepska Koliba, and they were engaged in the actions in order to verify the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard the interpreters asking me to repeat the question but you basically answered it. Therefore my question was whether you can confirm the information that part of the Zepa brigade, in organised manner, withdrew by swimming across the Drina and that other parts also went in the direction of Kladanj in an organised manner.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the information that was circulated at the time. Along with these forces that were pulling out towards Kladanj and securing the units on retreat, my unit was engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you one more thing in relation to the meeting at the Bratunac Brigade HQ that you attended to. We heard claims that at a meeting in the Bratunac Brigade, a decision was made that the VRS was to kill all men of military age moving in the column, both those who surrender and also those who wanted to proceed towards the free territory. Do you know anything about this, whether this was ever mentioned at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The third thing I wanted to ask you about refers to your notes. Can you tell me, did you keep those notes on a day-to-day basis and did you update them regularly about the events that happened on that day or did you take those notes occasionally after a couple of days and then recorded everything at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything depended on the time in the evening when I would return back, where part of the command was deployed. I didn't keep notes every evening. That's for sure. But I am certain that I didn't write about the events in Srebrenica in Zepa because these notes show that on the 13th, I gave tasks according to the schedule and the notes referring to the 12th were made on the 13th at the latest when I was drafting the tasks for the units that were supposed to move away from that area to a new area and my notes show the tasks that I was giving to particular officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, speaking about the tasks for the 11th, was that noted down on the 13th or maybe later or maybe before that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks for the 12th -- for the 11th and the 12th, after being issued in the area around the repeater, were noted down at the time when they were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, can you take a look at your notebook? It's 2D123, and pages 06085836, English version 1235. No, I'm sorry, 0605846. That's the 11th of July. 06085846. I can see that it's 2D123. Can we please then have the English version put up? And if necessary, we can have it on the ELMO as well. Can you please look at the 11th of July, second bullet, at 0950 hours, the commander of the Drina Corps, Major General Krstic issued tasks. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information that I have, the commander of the Drina Corps, the commander of the Drina Corps on the 11th of July was not Major General Krstic. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he wasn't, but I do allow for the possibility that this, of course, referred to the commander of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says very clearly here at 0950 hours --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's 0000 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 0900 hours, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is an abbreviation, TT, and that means commander, and DK means Drina Corps; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right in interpreting what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you for a different reason. According to our information, General Krstic became the Drina Corps commander somewhat later. I'm asking you is it possible that at the time when General Krstic became the Drina Corps commander, wrote this down?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It might have been a lapse in terms of thinking about the operation and the role, but it certainly wasn't written later on. I wouldn't have been able to compile all this information at a later stage. That was mentioned at the time when the axis and the combat areas were determined.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean your memory is not good enough for you to remember at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke in detail today and yesterday about the events that took place 12 years ago. If you couldn't remember such information only a few days later, how reliable will you say that your memory is about the events that took place 12 years ago?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please accept this explanation that I gave you, and that this was written on the day when the tasks were given. Due to an error on my part, I admit, I didn't even know that there was an order to appoint a commander of the corps before the lunch was organised, and definitely with regard to the command tasks, this remained written as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: By the way, I noticed that in no other document you never referred to General Krstic either as a commander of the corps or the commander of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That was just an accident or mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing: This refers to your trip to Krivaca on the 13th of July, 1995. You passed by a football stadium in Nova Kasaba. That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you pass in a car? What kind of car were you driving in?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- that was a PUCH. It's a jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a driver with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone else with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there was a Miss or a Mrs. from the organ for the moral guidance that was one of the departments in the command, and I think there was also a communications officer with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stop there or did you just pass by this football playground?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to stop in the area two or three times but I didn't alight from the vehicle. There were many curious people including reporters and camera crews, but I didn't get out of the vehicle because of the crowd and the jams on the road, it wasn't easy to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So that was on the road where the playground was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have seen this playground so we know exactly where the road is and where the playground is. I'm not particularly clear about a sentence that you mentioned. You didn't mention the specific number of people, but I am not clear about the assessment that you made in response to the request made by the Prosecution. I think you're not expected to give any estimates. You should rather speak about only what you saw or heard. As you said, there were about two people in a square metre to be multiplied by 100 and then again by 100. I didn't particularly understand how you made this calculation and what you exactly wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say anything. I didn't make any calculations to this date as to how many people it could have involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, and you said that they were guarded by some soldiers that some of them were in black uniforms and there were young soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention any black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I got it mixed up. So you mentioned some recruits or drafted young men who were just arrived.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about military policemen who were in the area at the time and one could conclude that they were securing the area. They were young and anyway, this battalion of the 65th protective regiment received new conscripts for training and on the basis of that, I concluded that they were members of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more question. Were you able to estimate how many soldiers were securing or guarding these detainees on the playground?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to say that, in my view, these men were disarmed enemy forces. They were not detainees. That's the first thing. Secondly, there were not too many of them since they were all sitting on the ground and they didn't pose any danger. I don't know how many soldiers were there. It was up to the commander to assess the number needed. Anyway, there were soldiers around the playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more question. Since you were sitting in the car and these people were sitting on the ground, I conclude that you didn't have the best view of the playground, given that you were probably -- obviously on the same level with them. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. One may conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Who wishes to go next? Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic, for sticking to your estimated time schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to just have you confirm several -- a couple things for me. Do you recall on October 5th, 2000, you gave a statement to the Tribunal, to the OTP investigator, and attorneys at the UN headquarters in Banja Luka? Do you recall that, sir, your first interview?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And during that interview, you were actually introduced to and questioned by Richard Butler. Do you recall Richard Butler, some military analyst that worked for the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the interview. I don't remember his face. He was introduced to me, and during the proofing session just now, I was reminded of the fact that it was Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And briefly, do you recall that he asked you whether or not you knew Colonel Ljubisa Beara and you answered, "Yes, I know"?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you further told him at the time that you did not see Colonel Beara in Potocari or Srebrenica area or any time following that in Zepa. I just want you to confirm that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, also, I'd like you to confirm that on the 24th day of January, 2004, you had another interview, this time with the representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor, being Mr. Peter McCloskey, who is here in the courtroom today, and a Ken Corlett from the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you recall that interview, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and I want to ask you do you recall this question being put to you by Mr. McCloskey, and it went like this? Mr. McCloskey asked you, sir, he said, "And not anywhere in the VRS does the security officer tell the brigade commander what to do, does he?" Do you remember him asking you that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: He further asked you, "or" meaning the security officer of the VRS, "Or do things behind his back," meaning the brigade commander's back. For the record, it's 2D122. In English it would be page 51, and the B/C/S -- and there's no line numbers on this, Your Honours. And the B/C/S, I really don't know what it is, what page it would be in B/C/S. Does that refresh your recollection at all about being asked that question?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you about your diary very briefly, to clarify one matter, that would be 2D125, English would be page 5, and B/C/S, I'm not sure. It's from the 900 hours, 12 July, 1995 is where it starts. And you make a notation that -- you're talking about Krstic, said, "You go ahead." You make a notation, "You want someone else to do your job. I replied to him that he is not of a strong principle to everyone (as he portrays himself) as he is towards me." Then you have written down, in all caps, "I am really clumsy commander." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And isn't it true, sir, that what you meant by that, being a clumsy commander, was -- and you actually have it written down, I think, the meaning is it's better to keep quiet or even to give false reports than to be a fair player in a game where human life is at stake. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You went on to state in your diary right after that, you made a notation that, "That's how you build a military career. However, I cannot do that." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Who is next? Mr. Bourgon? For the record, Ms. Nikolic, who wasn't here during part of the first session, is present now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I have a few questions for you and specifically to one area, something which you mentioned yesterday, and I'm quoting from page 65 of the transcript yesterday on lines 13 and 14. And you said at that moment, "If my superior were to come to the brigade command, he would first approach the brigade commander if he's there." Do you recall saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my superior was coming, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And further down on the same page, lines 18 to 20, you stated, "In any event, if any organ comes from a superior command, the brigade commander would be informed of this officer's coming to the command. That's a rule." Do you recall saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the sense that he would be informed either by the superior command or by the organs who were to receive that particular person in the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That was exactly the point I wanted to clarify with you. So either the officer visiting would inform the brigade commander, as is the custom, or your own assistant commander from your brigade, the person being visited, would inform you as brigade commander. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it is not possible to get in touch, the rule is to inform the commander after having had that meeting with somebody from the superior command. At any rate, the brigade commander has to be informed of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, of course, this rule, which you mentioned, there is a reason for this, and would I be right in saying that this is because as commander of the brigade, you want to be informed of everything that goes on in your brigade? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And of course, this applies in your absence to your Chief of Staff, he wants to know everything that's going on while you're away because he's standing in for you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd also like to confirm that no -- an assistant commander from a superior command could not issue an order to you as brigade commander. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, in fact, the only person that can issue an order to you is your superior commander, as brigade commander, I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And once again this applies -- the same applies to your Chief of Staff standing in, in your absence?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And lastly, if there was, to take an example, I suggest to you this also applies to your own assistant commanders whereby for example if the assistant commander for logistics coming from the corps was visiting your own assistant commander for logistics in the brigade, he could not issue an order to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, or he can ask that a certain assignment be performed, but the other person is required to tell him that he has to consult with his commander because he cannot engage units from the logistics support without the brigade commander knowing of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Again, this applies once again to your Chief of Staff in your absence?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thanks very much. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Nikolic. I take it therefore that there is no one else wishing to cross-examine this witness, correct? Do you have a re-examination? I would imagine you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. How long is it going to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll do my best to keep it at about half an hour. It may be longer. I will try to keep it at half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you decided what's going to happen with the next witness? Because -- yes, Mr. McCloskey? Because it's now quarter to 5.00. Half an hour, and that's being optimistic with you, having taken three times as much, if not four times as much with your examination-in-chief, it's very optimistic. So we finish this witness at 5.15. We have half an hour left and then three-quarters of an hour. That's one hour 15 minutes, which is short of the 2 hours and a half that at least they have indicated will be needed for the examination-in-chief with the next witness. That would mean if we are going to survive with him, you would have to cut down your cross-examination, but I will not impose it. He's an expert witness, and I will not impose anything on anyone. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have been -- I've spoken -- Mr. Vanderpuye will be doing the cross-examination of the expert. He is hoping, it's hard to say in this vacuum having not seen anything, he's hoping to be able to do it in two hours or less. So there is a chance we can finish. But if we cannot, I think this witness should be treated like any other witness and be required to come back on Tuesday and I don't see any other way around it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is, Mr. McCloskey, sorry to interrupt you like this, but at least to my knowledge, we were informed earlier on this week that he may face problems with his employers. He's going to be away on field trip for the duration of three months. That's the information that we have, at least. So I don't want to create problems to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are problem that has to be solved and I don't think he will be able to go back Sunday and obtain a visa Monday and return on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have tried to work out these issues with Defence counsel, and my -- and we have also heard that the visa problems had been resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. If that is the case, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, as I think Mr. Thayer had said, many times these -- once the Court -- or the Prosecution gets involved with employers, these employer problems aren't as bad as we thought. I think we need to really get to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- to ask him how serious that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed and then we see. All right. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you again, Mr. President. Good afternoon to Your Honours, good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified yesterday, and this was at page 72, line 1, that in your opinion, Krivaja 95 was hurriedly planned. Are you aware of an earlier operation in May of 1995 to close the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the command of the Drina Corps and the activities performed by the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I am, sir. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. May we have 65 ter 204 on e-court, please? Sir, do you have the image in front of you? Take a moment and read it, please, and when you're ready to have it scrolled up a little further, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can move on. Further down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: A little bit more. I don't think there is much left, sir. I think that's it for that page.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Further down. Further down. Further down. Down still.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
