utterances.text: That would be the next page, please. Is this ringing any bells, sir? Is it jogging your memory at all so far?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the time being, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except -- or, rather, it doesn't jog my memory because it does not relate to my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I was just going to try to move it along just a little bit. If we go to the page 3 of -- a little further down, to number 6, I think you'll see the reference to your unit, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then if we can go to the last page of the document, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I read his brigade name in -- on the first page as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see the signatory on this order, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy commander, Colonel Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. The -- on the first page that you read the heading was, "Order to stabilise defence around Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves and establish conditions for the liberation of the enclaves." And as His Honour just pointed out, it was addressed to a number of the brigade commands, including your own. Do you have any recollection of this order being issued?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that it reached the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But as to your recollection, do you have any recollection of this, this particular order for this particular operation in May of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the activities because the brigade had a task, which is referred to here, but I don't think this operation was planned much ahead. It must have been provoked by something that served as a basis for Colonel Krstic to take measures to take action with the forces holding positions facing the enclaves, forces of a smaller scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 205, please. And this is just a one-page document. Can you see that it's addressed, among others, to your unit and again signed by Colonel Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see the section, sir, that starts, "In relation to the order issued by the Drina Corps command, strictly confidential number 04/112"? And if you can just read the section that's --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Read the section beneath that, if you can read that out, please, and maybe that will help refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Due to a lack of insufficient -- of sufficient manpower" is that the paragraph you want me to read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Due to a lack of sufficient manpower, to fully close the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica and create conditions for the liberation of the enclaves, the foregoing order is supplemented and modified or rather amended as follows." Should I read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would just read paragraph 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2, item 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, item 2, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "First Milici Brigade and Vlasenica Brigade with a MUP unit will continue conducting reconnaissance and sweeping the terrain along the planned axis of engagement in accordance with the idea of the commanders of the 1st Milici and the 1st Vlasenica brigades with the coordination of the command of the Drina Corps with a view to fully gaining insight into enemy forces and their disposition in the gap between Zepa and Srebrenica and between Radava and Zelenica and Lisina. The Independent Battalion of Skelani will continue controlling the territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. Having read that paragraph as well, does that jog your memory at all as to this operation from the Drina Corps, this order that we talked about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents or measures taken by the deputy commander, and it is quite possible that the corps commander was absent at the time and he therefore discharged this role, these documents testify to regular activities because the Drina Corps considered this activity to be a regular activity which involved taking some measures. Since most of the forces of the Drina Corps were engaged in their positions opposite the enclaves, or were tied up with the enclaves, it often time happened that out of the area of these protected zones, sabotage actions were launched. It was a daily obligation to monitor the situation, collect intelligence, and prepare for active combat operations, regardless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. You can stop there. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am under the impression that this is a new examination-in-chief, rather than a follow-up on the cross-examination. I may be mistaken but some new matters were raised here like, for instance the month of May of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let Mr. Thayer respond to that. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we heard this testimony yesterday that Krivaja 95 was planned on very short notice, that there was insufficient intelligence concerning the locations and the axes, and I'm simply trying to find out whether the witness has any familiarity, recollection of another operation just a couple weeks prior in which some of these same areas are involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You can stop there. You can stop there. Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the Prosecutor refrain from using the term "operation," which has a specific meaning within the doctrine of the army of Republika Srpska? I'm certain that in time it will crop up that this is a very important matter. I appeal to him to use the term "actions" or any other terms but for the term "operation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Thayer? I think this has come up previously, although I don't remember it being determined. Do you wish to comment on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, number 1, there are references --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does it make any difference to you for the time being to refer to action rather than operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply using words that are used in the language of the document itself. So if the witness wishes to correct me on that in this particular instance I'm happy to be corrected, but I don't think we've been using the word "operation" loosely during this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau, I'm letting the witness follow this --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the proceedings, Your Honour, although -- I'm sorry, but in the version in B/C/S, there is no mention of the word "operation" and it's the same word in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know which word it would be in B/C/S, so I can't help you there. Anyway, let's not waste time on this issue. I mean, there is a divide between you on the use of this word. Please take it that whenever he's using "operation" it means "action." All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not sure you actually reached your answer but can you just tell us yes or no whether these documents refresh your recollection as to what was contained in this order and in the supplemental order that I showed you? If not, that's fine, and I'll just move on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to finish my sentence. Both documents, the order and the information linked to the previous document, reflects regular activities that the corps command is obliged to undertake. It is evident from the subheading or -- and the heading of the document, it has to do with stabilising the defence in the whole area facing the enclaves, and it also refers to the tasks thought about on a daily basis in order how to separate these forces by one's own actions. One should understand that throughout the period, there was contemplation of the need for this part of the encircled population in the enclave of how to liberate or how to demilitarise this. Since this was not done in compliance with the 1993 resolution of the Security Council and that constant losses were being sustained, it was only natural to think about the possibility of demilitarisation. This is my view. In other words, it doesn't involve any operation. It is merely a warning to the units that they -- that defence deserve more attention in this area and that they should, with their action, impart on the 28th Division that they are not going to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you ever receive information or did you ever become aware that just a couple of weeks after these two orders, the VRS attacked and captured the UNPROFOR observation post Echo located near Zeleni Jadar on June 3rd, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning this activity, I have no recollection. There may have been information to that effect but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine. And having spent some of the time that you did in the operation at Srebrenica, did you have any understanding of the importance of securing that communication that ran south, just south of the enclave near Zeleni Jadar which the VRS was able to do when they took over that observation post?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any details about that. My unit was not connected with this. I didn't receive tasks of that kind. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. You were asked some questions by my learned friend Ms. Fauveau yesterday about whether you'd seen a map with certain unit positions and movements drawn on it, and you answered that you believe that you did recall seeing it. And that was at page 37, line 1. If we may have 65 ter 1499 displayed, this is going to take a couple of minutes, probably, because it's a very detailed map and frankly I don't know if it's going to show up well enough, but I have a full-size copy here, with Madam Usher's assistance. Okay. And if we may have the top half of the map blown up, if we could zoom in on that, please? Okay. You see the image there, sir? And if it also helps you, if you want to un -- apologies to Madam Usher, but if you want to unfold the map to take a look at it in its entirety, please feel free to do so because I think the image on the screen is pretty good, but if you would unfold it and feel free to look at the bottom half, too. Now, on the portion that's on the screen right now, and I think you're looking at the same portion that's on the ELMO there, but the top portion of the screen here is the Srebrenica enclave; is that correct? And I want you to just identify, if you could --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- a couple of markings. On top of the enclave, there appears to be a cross with four Cs. I'll ask you about that in a second, but if you look in the lower right-hand quadrant of that cross, there are some markings, the abbreviation 1 PB and 2 PB. Do you see where I'm referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know what those markings refer to, based on looking at this map?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these abbreviations, this indicates infantry battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you were serving in the Srebrenica operation, the battalion-size groups that were formed, were they given a number during the operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do these particular battalion markings and the directions indicated next to them suggest anything to you concerning the Srebrenica operation and the movements of the VRS troops during it? There appear to be arrows moving to the north west of Zeleni Jadar marked 1st Battalion, other arrows moving more due west, marked 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are marks -- markings and axis of activities that someone was contemplated, I presume, and I see that the name of Krstic is named here, but I cannot establish any connection with the operation in which I took part.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does the marking of the 1st Battalion, is that consistent with the movements of your forces, sir? The arrow that is shown there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell the Court what this cross mark with the four letters represents that's over the Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness says that he cannot establish any connection with the operation in which he took part. Therefore I don't see the point of asking further questions with regard to this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm asking him whether he recognises what that symbol is, Your Honour. It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We see no problem with that question. Go ahead if you can answer that question, please, Mr. Trivic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This cross and four Ss, yes, four letters S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does that represent anything to you, sir? Do you recognise that as having any particular meaning?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the map itself and what General Krstic signed indicates that it's a Serbian map, that Srebrenica has been and remained Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that in fact what you read in the handwriting to the right of the portion of the map you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've just read that it reads, "Srebrenica was and is still Serbs." And the date is the 12th of July, and I think this is how he was thinking and planning, and this symbol of 4 Ss was probably added later on. But it has nothing to do with the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you see any signature anywhere on the map, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you read the signature?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major General Rad Krstic, and that's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is there any significance when a general signs a map?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is his personal map that he was using, and it reflects his thoughts about something, but as a combat document, I've never laid eyes on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So this is from your recollection not the map that you saw on that occasion that you referred to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I didn't receive interpretation, but I think I understood it well enough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- that it's been asked and answered twice or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I apologise to you, but usually when Madam Fauveau speaks, I follow her in French, and the fact that interpretation did not filter through escaped me completely.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises for not switching on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, it's -- I apologise, I apologise too. So Mr. Thayer, it's a suggestion by Ms. Fauveau is that this has been asked twice and -- has been asked and has already been answered, so what's your position on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My position is he's indicated he's not familiar with it, but I just wanted to put it to rest that whether or not this is the map that he saw in -- on the occasion that he described earlier. It's just a simple yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Mr. Trivic, let's clarify this once and for all. Have you seen this map before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If we could scroll this map a bit to the right, further and further down, and then down, down, down, down, yes. Further down. If you could ask the witness to read this part as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That was the last question I had on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you read what's written there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. "Zepa is Serbian too, 27th July, 1995, Major General Rad Krstic," signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on, sir. I want to turn your attention to directive 7 which you were asked a number of questions about yesterday. And you were read a portion, and this is at page 10 of the English and page 15 of the B/C/S, 65 ter number 5, the portion under the Drina Corps tasking, part of it reads, "By planned and well-thought-out combat operations create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." Now, you testified yesterday that you don't interpret this as a plan of attack on a civilian population. Are you aware of any efforts undertaken by the VRS to make life unbearable for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa, to create a situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life? Are you aware of any efforts undertaken by the VRS in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I'm not aware of any such effort aimed at achieving this as described in this portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now I want to turn -- I'm sorry. I thought you were finished.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, witness, since there was this small interruption, the interpreters didn't catch up your last words. If you could kindly repeat them, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally am not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. At page 14 of this document, directive 7, which is page 21 of the B/C/S, there is a portion, I'll just move it along, I'll just read it: "The relevant state and military organs responsible for work with UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations shall, through the planned and unobtrusively restrictive issuing of permits reduce and limit the logistics support of UNPROFOR to the enclaves and the supply of material resources to the Muslim population, making them dependent on our goodwill while at the same time avoiding condemnation by the international community and international public opinion." Now, sir, do you know which Main Staff assistant commander, if any, was primarily responsible for liaison with international organisations and with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who was designated to do that job.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know which Main Staff assistant commander was primarily responsible for approving and denying UNPROFOR and UNHCR conveys to the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because through the defence zone of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, these routes did not run, and I don't know who was responsible and who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, were you aware of any plan or operation directed by the VRS to cut off the resupply of DutchBat and to restrict the inflow of humanitarian aid to the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, although by reading the book "Srebrenica: Chronicle of a Crime" or something like that, written by members of the DutchBat, one may draw conclusions -- a conclusion that there were certain problems but that on the other hand, there were certain agreements and that it did work with difficulties but the supply lines were operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let's move along. I want to turn to a new topic. With respect to the Srebrenica operation, in response to the VRS attack on the enclaves, were you ever informed or advised during the course of the preparation or the operation, if NATO came in, in support of UNPROFOR, either with air strikes or reinforcement, reinforcements, was there a plan to engage in combat with those NATO elements?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. May we have 65 ter 107, please? Sir, this is the attack plan that you've been asked a lot of questions about. I would just turn your attention, if we could have page 4 of the original, that's page 6 of the English, and we will be focusing on paragraphs 8 and 9, please. Thank you. Do you see the portion under "anti-aircraft defence" where it says, "In case of a NATO air strike have material for anti-aircraft operations in all units open fire on low flying planes that threaten the order of battle"? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I see it, but I would like to go back to the title of this document. This is not an order to attack but an order to carry out active activities, which is substantially different. I've seen this and -- but why I said I didn't see this, my unit didn't have any anti-aircraft equipment and quite simply we didn't organise any anti-aircraft defence within my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show -- turn your attention to paragraph 9 where it says, "Anti-airborne-landing combat: If NATO forces make an airborne landing in support of UNPROFOR, the units closest to the landing place and reserve forces will engage in combat with them. Artillery and armoured mechanised units will support an anti-airborne-landing combat at the given signal." Sir, do you remember ever being informed of this aspect of the plan?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that this order was drafted according to the pattern that was used as a standard form and that it was a normal practice. It doesn't speak or doesn't give us any particular information and there it is similar to other orders of this nature that were issued. This was the standard procedure of assigning tasks to units, and on the basis of the knowledge that anti-aircraft defence is supported by artillery and other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. May we have 65 ter 108 displayed, please? Do you see that document in front of you, sir? It's from the Drina Corps command dated 5 July to all subordinate units and it specifically refers to, "In view of possible actions by NATO air forces and rapid reaction forces around the enclaves and in particular around the Srebrenica enclave." Do you see the order section?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see where it says, "In particular, be prepared to use all available weapons against helicopters of the rapid reaction forces in order to prevent them flying over the front line and threatening our forces in depth"? Do you see that, sir? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And how about paragraph 2 where it says "open fire on planes and helicopters without requesting special authorisation"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. This line of questioning goes beyond the framework of the cross-examination. Nowhere in my -- or in the cross-examination was there any mention of NATO forces or rapid reaction forces but, rather, UNPROFOR and these are two different things. There were both UNPROFOR and NATO forces or rather rapid reaction forces in Bosnia. Therefore, this question goes beyond my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was lengthy examination on cross-examination as to how UNPROFOR, UN forces were to be treated with maximum protection and that the UN and UNPROFOR were not targets of this operation and I'm simply asking this witness whether he remembers receiving certain orders with respect, as I asked him, to what would happen if there were reinforcements or air support in connection with those forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really think that one ought to distinguish between UNPROFOR forces and NATO forces which were the aggressor on the territory of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer, do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, not on that, Mr. President. I don't think we need to go down that road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We believe that this has been answered already in one way or another. Let's move, Mr. Thayer, and you have exceeded already the three-quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour. I'm trying to keep it moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In ten minutes time we have a break. I enjoin you to try to bring your cross -- your re-examination to a close as soon as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They have taken it as a joke.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's a Freudian slip. I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked on Monday a very specific question by my friend, Mr. Krgovic at page 11883, line 17: "Are you aware of the existence of a plan on the part of some of the UNPROFOR officials to use helicopter flights around Srebrenica to provoke the VRS soldiers into opening fire at helicopters which would then be used as an excuse for bombing the VRS forces?" And you answered that you had and that you had examined some documents and statements by certain members of UN forces and then specifically identified General Smith as, in your words, the person who was in favour of provoking the VRS fire against the aircraft involved in the distribution of the humanitarian aid to the area. Now, and you reiterated that yesterday and again in your testimony yesterday you specifically referred to studying some documents in coming to your conclusion, in addition to General Smith's statement. And you referred on a number of occasions to reviewing documents and materials. First, just quickly, sir, what other cases have you served as a defence expert or consultant or assisted in? And the reason I'm asking is I just want to know, have you been provided with documents, reports and statements in connection with your work in those other cases that are pertinent to the events in Srebrenica in July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not state that I was aware of the plan. I said that there were statements to that effect, and one of the statements referred to by the authors of the book "Our Dear War Criminals" contains or rather refers to a statement by General Smith that he asked representatives of UN forces to provoke the Serb side or, rather, the -- any sort of fire upon helicopters bringing in humanitarian aid in order to provide him with the basis for the engagement of the air forces to engage and strike Serbian positions. Secondly, I wish to comment upon the two documents I have just seen. When thinking about the possible threats of dangers, they were considering the positions of the VRS forces in and around enclaves, that they might be exposed to NATO air strikes. This is what they were considering. And I think that for this reason, they thought that they ought to protect their forces. This is just a normal line of thinking on the part of a commander, to envisage all sorts of threats that may befall their forces and to take measures accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do you remember actually being given the statement of General Smith to the Office of the Prosecutor and whether that was what you were referring to? Or are you just referring to the two books that you just told us about only?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also read General Smith's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So let me just see if this is what you remember reading. This is General Smith's statement at page 10, B/C/S page 11, "Throughout April the situation in Bosnia deteriorated further. The enclaves continued to be squeezed logistically to the extent that I made a further plan to resupply the enclaves by helicopter, daring the BSA to attack a helicopter with the prospect of subsequent air attack. This plan was put to the UNHQs in Zagreb and New York but was seen as too risky and confrontational." Was that the statement you remember reading, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly. I believe that something is missing in the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Something is missing in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't help you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I can show the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you go through your last part of -- or the entire question? Which part is missing, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: "Daring the BSA to attack helicopters with the prospect of subsequent air attack."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No. The statement -- I'll reread the statement, then. That's a misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you could kindly --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- do that, please, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And it's just -- everything was correct except -- it's "with the prospect of subsequent air attack."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What would be the correct -- your correct statement in English, during -- daring the BSA -- daring the BSA to attack a helicopter? What did you actually say?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What I read literally, Your Honour, was: "The enclaves continue to be squeezed logistically to the extent that I made a further plan to resupply the enclaves by helicopter, daring the BSA to attack a helicopter with the prospect of subsequent air attack."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Is it clear now? Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's clear, but I have the statement in B/C/S that's quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how is it different, if you could explain, because we don't understand the language?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may read it out, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "During April the situation in Bosnia further deteriorated. The enclaves were logistically squeezed to such an extent that I created a new plan for supplying the enclaves by helicopter. This was a daring to the army of Republika Srpska, challenging the army of Republika Srpska to attack the enclaves so that then we would strike them."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't say anything more than I'm reading the English statement as it was written by the investigator. So if we are getting things lost in translation, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not a native English speaker, as you know, and I feel a little bit lost in trying to find a difference between the two versions. Perhaps Mr. Josse or Mr. Haynes can help us. Yes, unless Madam Fauveau has polished her English to an extent that she can resolve the whole question for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, but I am increasingly concerned. I believe that this statement by General Smith was not correctly interpreted into the B/C/S, and a moment ago we had a very important document that was not in -- translated well from the B/C/S into English, and we will not make much headway if the Prosecutor bases his submissions on the English versions and we on the B/C/S versions. I believe that this calls for a serious comparison and checking of all translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That will be done in the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Mr. Thayer and I have had some discussion about this extract over the last few days, and I came to the conclusion that there might be a translation problem. In other words, of course the original of general Smith's statement is in English, it has therefore been translated into B/C/S, there might be a problem. We haven't had that sorted out yet. It might take a bit of time, but basically I'm supporting what Madam Fauveau is saying, there may be a difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She's 100 per cent right. If the translation doesn't reflect verbatim the English version, it may well be B/C/S version or rendering of what is the English -- the original in English, but not necessarily an exact translation thereof. So we need to -- but in this case, I don't see much difference between what is contained in the English original and what has been read by Mr. Krgovic and translated to us into English. I mean, the bottom line at the end, at the end, the substance is there. They are both saying the same thing. So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, just one last question on this issue of what you read that led you to your conclusion regarding the purpose of the helicopter resupply plan. As part of the materials that you've reviewed in connection with your service as an expert or consultant, were you ever given a copy of the 1999 UN report to the General Assembly? And that's 65 ter 528. Do you recall that, whether you were ever given that document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just read you a portion of that and see if that is a document that you may have been given and if it's consistent with what you're basing your interpretation on. This is at page 45, paragraph 184: "As the military situation deteriorated, the Serbs further restricted access to the eastern enclaves, both for UNPROFOR and for the international humanitarian organisations. For the UNPROFOR units within the enclaves, this lack of access caused a degradation of their military capability while for the local population the result was a further worsening of living conditions. The UNPROFOR commander in Bosnia-Herzegovina proposed that the enclaves be resupplied by helicopter with NATO air power to be used if the Serbs attempted to intercept any of the helicopters. His superior in Zagreb, the force commander, assessed that there was a considerable likelihood that the Serbs would indeed fire upon the helicopters and thus sought the views of the member states whose troops or air assets would be required to conduct the operation. Those states did not respond favourably." Do you remember being furnished with this report or reading any material that is consistent with this report, sir? And if so, is it consistent or not with your interpretation of the purpose of the resupply-by-helicopter plan?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report is consistent in the part which mentions that there were proposals to bring in humanitarian supplies by helicopters and that there was the threat of the escalation of confrontations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to turn to an area of discussion yesterday concerning command, and I've narrowed it down considerably but I want to get to a couple of primary points, important points that were raised yesterday. You were asked some questions about when you were in the field and who was in charge back in your brigade, and you identified your Chief of Staff as being that individual. Now, sir, when you were in the field, how important was it for you, as brigade commander, to communicate with that Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My Chief of Staff in my absence from the command post carried out all the activities in accordance with my decision on the engagement of units. He was to settle certain matters with regard to logistics, and in all matters he continued to carry out all the tasks he was aware of pursuant to my decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor please specify whether his question had to do with the absence of the commander within the area of responsibility of the brigade or when the commander is absent outside that area? Or rather he is outside that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm actually getting to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau, and thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you were in the field, whether inside your area or outside your area, what types of information would it be important for your Chief of Staff, who was in charge in your place, to communicate to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will go back to my explanation of this relationship that I gave back in Banja Luka in the UN office, namely about the relationship and in what situation is he required to ask my opinion. Well, he's required to do that only when something changes in relation to my decision is the Chief of Staff required to inform me or to inform the superior command and ask for their position to get feedback from them and see whether he has the approval for changing my decision. Since I have not been through such situations as these, my Chief of Staff never had occasion or need to get in touch with me for any changes in matters to be taken care of concerning my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, given your experience, who is the first superior commander or superior officer that your Chief of Staff should try to contact in such a circumstance?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, he should get in touch with me, if that is possible. If that's not possible, then he should contact the superior command, with the person who approved my decisions, and that's the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about superior command officers arriving at your brigade and beginning to conduct business there. Do you remember those questions?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I -- you testified that -- this is at page 65. You were asked the question, "When officers from superior command came to the brigade, you didn't have the right or power to stop them doing their job at the brigade, did you?" And you answered, "I didn't say that if they announced their arrival I can stop them or prevent them from doing their job. At any rate, they would do their part of the job with the organ who was his functioning corresponding post. Of course, the commander would not prevent him from doing his duty, but it is the rule that such an arrival has to be announced." Now, my question, sir, is: How about if these officers from the superior command arrived at your brigade and their business or their job or the work they were doing involved something illegal, involved illegal orders or illegal activity? Number one, if you were there in the brigade, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Does that question presuppose that he knows that they were up to anything illegal? I think that ought to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We agree. I don't know if you wish to comment on that, but we fully agree with what Mr. Haynes has pointed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. I presume he can't act if he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So the question is: If you were made aware that this illegal conduct or illegal orders are being issued by or through these superior command officers, what do you do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a hypothetical question. The witness is asked to speculate in theory. It is not his experience based on the duties he performed at the time that is sought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the first instance, there was a fair amount of expert opinion that was elicited, I would respectfully submit, through this witness. Secondly, I'm not asking for an expert opinion. I'm asking based on his experience, his knowledge, his training, his service in the army, his knowledge of the regulations, his understanding of his duties and responsibilities as a brigade commander, what was he to do in that circumstance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't agree that the witness is being asked to speculate, Ms. Nikolic. So based on what your experience and knowledge of the circumstances were, could you kindly answer the question now, Mr. Trivic, please? And I don't think we need to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If somebody from the superior command to carry out something in coordination with an organ of the command or the command itself, to carry out something illegal, I believe it is only natural that I wouldn't allow such a thing to happen, and I would take measures, disciplinary and other measures, against the officer involved, any such measures as are envisaged for such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the situation where you're in the field, whether you're out of your area or within your area, but if you yourself return to your brigade and you learn that members of your own brigade are engaging in criminal conduct or they've been following illegal orders issued from a higher command, is your answer the same or would you do something different?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the same in both situations. My duty would be to inform the superior command about what had happened and what measures I had taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, if such illegal activity had been underway in your brigade and your Chief of Staff had knowledge of it while you were in the field, in your experience, what would you expect him to do with that information?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would expect him to act in the same manner, within the scope of duties and responsibilities of all officers, including the brigade Chief of Staff. The duties is to undertake identical measures. There are no different rules applicable to officers and commanding staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who would you expect to be the first person he would contact with respect to that information of illegal conduct or illegal orders within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, your Chief of Staff, sir, who you've been referring to.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first person that he should inform about is the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that would be you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to turn to another area. You were asked the following question yesterday. Actually -- well, I'll just read the question: "In July of 1995, there was no need whatsoever for anyone to stand in for General Milovanovic in his position of Chief of Staff of the VRS."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question read by the Prosecutor was indeed asked, but it was withdrawn. In actual fact it wasn't asked at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President, but there had been prior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I recollect as well, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- prior discussion about what standing in and those types of terms meant. There was substantial questioning about whether General Milovanovic was standing in at a particular time and who was in command, and I just want to ask a couple of questions on that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me clear this. From my memory - and I stand to be corrected - but usually I'm not wrong when I try to remember. The question that Ms. Fauveau had asked the witness was the following: "And when General Milovanovic was not around, was not available, or in any case, could General Miletic take decisions independently?" Now, at that point in time you stood up and made some kind of objection, without belittling your objection, and Madam Fauveau's response was, "Okay, I withdraw the question." It's true that you withdrew the question, but the question, the previous questions that you had put basically were along the -- constituted a series of questions of within the chain of command what would happen in the absence of or the unavailability of one of the commanders. And it wasn't just you who had hinted at this on this issue, but also others who had put questions. So I think at this point in time, I will consult my colleagues --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This question was -- this particular question was asked and answered, page 44, line 13. It was a subsequent question that was, I think, withdrawn. So there has been testimony. I don't think we are saying anything different, but I just wanted to put on the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There was definitely questions by Madam Fauveau on General Milovanovic, whether General Miletic was subordinate to General Milovanovic and where was General Milovanovic at some point in time, so I think -- I think I need to consult with my colleagues before we hand down our ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may be shown 65 ter 44, please? Sir, this is -- do you see an image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report from the Main Staff dated July 12th, 1995. If we could turn to the third page, please, it's the last page, of the B/C/S, and if we could scroll down to the bottom, sir, this daily combat report was sent, in addition to the corps command, to the president of the Republika Srpska, and I just ask to you look at the signature line in the lower left-hand corner, and can you read what that says, sir, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads, "standing in for the Chief of Staff, Major General Radivoje Miletic."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, what does that term mean to you, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This suggests that General Miletic in this area, discharged duties in terms of collecting information from subordinate units, processing this information and forwarding it to the relevant quarters or recipients named in the preamble of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. I'll spare you showing you some other examples of these. If we could have P02497? Do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's dated 18 June 1995. It's with respect to approvals and convoy routes for three UNPROFOR convoys. Can we turn to the second page of the original, please? Again there is some handwriting in the lower left-hand corner above the time stamp box. Can you read what that says?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Standing in for NSH, Colonel Radivoje Miletic".

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you to read the large paragraph, please, that appears on this page, if you could just read that into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no objection to the witness reading this document, but in that case, it will be necessary for him to read it in its entirety, because this passage was totally taken out of context and it does not reflect the whole of the document in a proper way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long is the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's two pages. And the first page is simply convoy routes, dates and times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll give the opportunity to the witness to go through the document as quickly as he can, concentrating on what is relevant to the question basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may help the Prosecution and the witness, I would be satisfied only to hear the first sentence on the first page be read out and then we can move on to this particular paragraph on page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that. The first paragraph on the first page, we can see, although we can't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you read that, sir, just please read it out, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Open text, "Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there. I think my learned friend was referring to the first sentence - I'm sorry - under where it says "military post 7111," if you do just read that line, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We hereby inform you that we have approved the movement of UNPROFOR convoy from Zagreb via Belgrade to the enclaves according to the following."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. May we have the second page now, please? And sir, would you please read that large paragraph? And I just want to ask you a couple of quick questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I demand that all vehicles be searched thoroughly, which involves the checking of the freight being transported, particularly fuel in fuel tanks and fuel transported to the enclaves. Also check the documents and particularly pay attention to checking the identity of all individuals, making the list of their names and their ID cards in order to ensure that the individuals entering the enclaves will -- shall leave the enclaves after their mission is completed."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified yesterday that General Miletic could not issue orders, and that was at page 43, line 16. Is there a difference between originating an order and passing an order, or passing on an order?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a crucial difference, and it's reflected in this document. These orders were not issued. They do not encroach on the Krivaja 95 decisions. They do not interfere with the decisions of the commander of the Main Staff, but, rather, this is a notice going out to the commands, in this case to the military post, and it is a request for the military post to carry out this task in line with this instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. My only question on this document at this time, then, is: When the chief of operations and training of the Main Staff of the VRS who's standing in for the Chief of Staff issues a document which says, "I demand a detailed control of all vehicles," with further instructions in it and this gets distributed, as it did to your brigade, as we can see from the first page, how free would you feel to disregard that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that this refers to the procedures that both sides had to adhere to when these convoys were passing through, and I don't see anything here that bears relevance to combat activities. These were standard procedures to be observed and everyone involved was aware of those procedures. There was an agreement that particular attention should be paid to specific issues during the passage of the convoy on account of certain suspicions that there were certain activities that were contrary to the established procedures, in some previous instances of similar nature in some previous convoy passages.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm not asking you about combat activity in this sentence. I'm asking you if you had not followed these procedures as demanded in this paragraph, what would the consequences have been, if you had permitted these vehicles simply to go through?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no mention here of units. This refers to the military post 7111. This notice was addressed to it, as was the demand for it to adhere to proper procedure. And I don't know if they complied.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, what do you think would have happened if they didn't comply, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's inconceivable that they wouldn't comply. They were informed what they were supposed to do, and I presume that they reported back about what they did to the Main Staff, and that would be the information or report recorded as mission completed by Colonel --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the name of the colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just repeat the name, sir, mission completed by Colonel? The interpreter didn't pick up the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was the colonel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel Radivoje Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified on -- I want to go into another area -- on Monday that your unit did not fire on the town of Srebrenica, that you didn't observe, notice or hear any other units firing upon the town of Srebrenica. Were you ever provided with any UN documents, such as UN military observer reports or statements of Dutch soldiers, humanitarian organisation employees or Muslim civilians who were in Srebrenica and Potocari during the VRS attack?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At any time, were you provided with any such documents concerning statements or information from any of the types of people I just identified who were in Srebrenica and Potocari during the time of the VRS attack? For example, while you were engaged in your operation.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my engagement in the Krivaja 95 operation, I didn't receive any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, again, I'll spare you going through a number of such UNMO reports. There is just one I want to go through in the time we have left. You testified that when you were in Srebrenica town on the 11th and 12th, you didn't see any evidence of artillery fire there and, in particular, you saw no evidence of damage from shells to the hospital. I just want to just read to you from 65 ter 501. It's a UN situation report dated the 10th of July at 12.55 p.m.: "Two heavy shells, probably 155-millimetre artillery shells hit the direct surrounding of the hospital at 1100 hours. All the windows are smashed and shrapnel has showered the walls and rooms of the hospital. It looks as if the BSA are now targeting the hospital and the surroundings." Sir, first of all, what kind of weapon fires a 155-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am an artillery man, and if you're asking me a technical question, because it doesn't say here that it was a 155-millimetre but that it was probably this shell, then I presume it must have been fired from a 155-millimetre howitzer gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you never received any of that information, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You never saw the glass on the ground, I guess; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were broken windows. I don't know what kind of buildings we are talking about but there were no destroyed buildings. The hospital wasn't destroyed. It says close to the hospital, in close proximity of the hospital. So the building itself was not demolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Finally, sir, you testified about informing superior command about conducting asanacija, and can we have 65 ter number 219 displayed, please? If we could have page 24 of the original? Sir, this, as you can see from the title, is a reports and meetings of the 1st Bratunac light Infantry Brigade. The page I'm going to have displayed at page 11 is dated 16 October 1995. If we could scroll down to the bottom, do you see the entry that says "Nikolic"?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just for the record, we are not representing that this has anything -- that this refers to the accused, Drago Nikolic, in this reference to Nikolic. Do you see the last line there, sir? Can you just read what it says?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last line reads, "We are currently involved in carrying out the duties given by the GSH VRS (asanacija)."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the translation in the transcript and what my learned colleague said is inconsistent. I think this has to do with the Bratunac Brigade, if I'm not mistaken. However, in the B/C/S interpretation, it was said that this refers to the accused Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It says, just for the record, we are not representing -- basically we are not asserting that this has anything to anything to do, that this refers, to the accused Drago Nikolic. I think it's clear enough. You don't have to worry about it. Neither has your client. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And sir, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That abbreviation, GSH VRS, what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever become aware of any operation to dig up and rebury bodies of thousands of Muslim men and boys from Srebrenica who had been executed following the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you were asked about how asanacija is supposed to be done as a matter of humanitarian rights of people, care for their families, human dignity and due piety. Can we be shown P02103, page 246, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the top of the page indeed it shows P02103, so-- the screen, sorry, not the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's just loading up, I think, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you have an image on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, it's the Prosecution's position that this is a photograph of a mass grave exhumed north of Zvornik and it contains the bodies of some of those men and boys. Is this consistent with the human dignity and due piety that you described asanacija requiring for burying the dead?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. Of course, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions for you at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to ask the Trial Chamber's permission to put one or two questions to the witness about a document that the Prosecutor showed to the witness and which constituted a continuation of my cross-examination which I did not wish to pursue upon a request by the Prosecution. And I promise it will not take more than a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we are already past 7.00, Madam Fauveau. It's two minutes past the hour already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically that means the witness has to return tomorrow for two minutes or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. You've got two minutes and we finish because the witness has to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Could the witness be shown Exhibit P2488? Further cross-examination by Ms. Fauveau:

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before this exhibit comes up, before General Miletic signs a document as the person standing in for the Chief of Staff, is it not true that the contents of that document have to be in accordance with the instructions issued by the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This number cannot be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She doesn't need the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I will need the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you repeat your answer? It was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It has to be in accordance with the instructions issued by the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your consideration, Madam Fauveau. Witness, I won't keep you any longer. Thank you for having come over to give testimony. On behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We stand adjourned until tomorrow at the same time, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
